item.title: Akita Museum of Art: Foujita's Mural & Tadao Ando — Guide
item.description: The Akita Museum of Art, designed by Tadao Ando, is home to Tsuguharu Foujita’s monumental mural ‘Events in Akita’ — one of the largest canvases in Japan, depicting the prefecture’s festivals and daily life. Ando’s spiral staircase and a rooftop triangular water pool that frames Senshu Park make the building itself a work of art. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Akita City, Akita Hours ~10:00–18:00 (closed irregular) Admission Around ¥310 (collection) Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round What to See Foujita’s vast mural ‘Events in Akita’.

item.title: Naoshima Art Island, Kagawa: The Complete Visitor's Guide
item.description: Naoshima is a small island of roughly 8 square kilometres in the Seto Inland Sea, about 50 minutes by ferry from Takamatsu. In the early 1990s, it was a quiet island with an ageing fishing population, a modest industrial presence, and no particular reason to appear on any travel itinerary. Over the following three decades, the Fukutake Foundation — the philanthropic arm of Benesse Holdings, based in Okayama — transformed it into one of the world’s most celebrated destinations for contemporary art and architecture.
